title.narrative: Accelerating Cabo Verde's Transition to Blue and Green Economy

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Table 8. Project alignment with pillars for decent rural employment Alignment of project activities with the FAO's 4 pillars for Decent Rural Employment Project Components 1. Integration of nature into development and fiscal policies and planning of key economic sectors Project Outcomes Project Outputs Alignment with FAO’s decent rural employment pillars Activities in the project Comments 1.1 Ecosystems Services Valuation (ESV) informs monitoring of ecosystems, sustainable agriculture, tourism, and fisheries decision-making 1.1.1 Ecosystem service valuation conducted in target PAs and buffer zones Pillar 1 Employment creation and enterprise development Issue 1.1.1 Employment-enhancing agricultural and rural development polices and strategies Assign economic values to natural resources and ecosystem services involving various valuation methods, such as market prices, replacement cost, contingent valuation and fishing resources rent, in usable ways to be accessed by intersectoral stakeholders in decision-making Support satellite accounts development and the National Institute of Statistics (INE) to focus on natural capital. These accounts will include physical, monetary, and interactive information related to natural resources, providing policymakers and researchers with detailed insights into the state and trends of natural capital. Integrate natural capital accounting results into policy development and decision-making processes through specific recommendations This activity contributes to the development of employment-enhancing agricultural and rural development policies by providing insights into the economic contributions of natural resources and ecosystem services to rural economies. Understanding the economic value of these resources can inform policies that prioritize sustainable resource management, leading to the creation of jobs in sectors such as sustainable agriculture, agroforestry, and eco-tourism. Developing satellite accounts focusing on natural capital provides policymakers with detailed insights into the state and trends of natural resources. This information can be used to design employment-enhancing policies that promote the sustainable use of natural resources. For example, policymakers can identify areas for investment in rural infrastructure, such as irrigation systems or renewable energy projects, which can create employment opportunities in construction and maintenance. Integrating natural capital accounting results into policy development ensures that employment-enhancing strategies are informed by the sustainable management of natural resources. Policymakers can use this information to develop targeted interventions that support rural employment, such as training programs for sustainable agriculture practices or incentives for green businesses. By incorporating natural capital considerations into policy decisions, employment opportunities in rural areas can be maximized while ensuring environmental sustainability. 1.1.2 Integrated and comprehensive terrestrial and marine sustainable development and investment plans in target PAs and their buffer zones benefitting vulnerable communities Pillar 4 Governance and social dialogue Issue4.2.1 Representation and empowerment of the rural poor, particularly women and youth, in social dialogue and policy dialogue through rural workers’ organizations, producers’ organizations and civil society organizations Support existing, and establish where missing, multi-stakeholder committees in each protected area, representative of livelihood and natural resource user groups Design investment plans for targeted protected areas (potentially financed through vehicles identified under Component 3) to respond to sustainability needs with a clear rationale for livelihoods, economic advancement, revenue generation, and social development with a green and blue economy approach This activity directly aligns with the goal of representation and empowerment by ensuring that rural communities, particularly marginalized groups such as women and youth, have a voice in decision-making processes related to protected areas. By including these stakeholders in multi-stakeholder committees, their perspectives, needs, and concerns can be addressed in policies and decisions affecting their livelihoods. This empowerment through representation fosters social dialogue and ensures that policies are inclusive and responsive to the needs of all community members. Designing investment plans for protected areas with a focus on sustainability and livelihoods supports the empowerment of rural communities, ad builds economies for their future. These plans can incorporate strategies that promote economic advancement and social development while ensuring the conservation of natural resources. For example, investments in eco-tourism infrastructure can create employment opportunities for local communities, particularly women and youth, while also preserving the natural environment. Additionally, integrating a green and blue economy approach emphasizes sustainable practices that benefit both people and the environment. By including marginalized groups in social and policy dialogues and investing in initiatives that benefit their communities, these activities help to create a more inclusive and equitable rural development framework, in which people play a part in their own socioeconomic development. 1.1.3 Integrated ecosystems monitoring and reporting systems operational at local, regional and national levels Pillar 4 Issue4.2.1 Representation and empowerment of the rural poor, particularly women and youth, in social dialogue and policy dialogue through rural workers’ organizations, producers’ organizations and civil society organizations Support the uptake of technology and provide capacity building on devices such as mobile apps, sensors, and online platforms to facilitate data collection, submission, and analysis among tourism, agriculture and fisheries stakeholders. Utilize user-friendly tools that align with the local context and technical capabilities of participants There is a potential that improved ecosystems monitoring can enhance protection of natural resources which are used for peoples’ livelihoods. There are also opportunities for creating new roles and paid partnerships between government and local communities, or researchers, universities and populations to monitor the state of ecosystems by local citizenry. 1.2. Improved inter-sectoral governance mechanisms support nature-positive decision-making 1.2.1 Multi-stakeholder policy dialogues strengthened to support policy coherence locally and nationally Pillar 4 Issue4.2.1 Representation and empowerment of the rural poor, particularly women and youth, in social dialogue and policy dialogue through rural workers’ organizations, producers’ organizations and civil society organizations Create a Multistakeholder Dialogue Forum for protected areas including the Parliamentary Committee for the Environment, MAA-DNA, DGASP, MM-DNPA, IMAR, Ministry of Tourism, NGOs, Community-based associations, ICIEF and key private stakeholders in the tourism, agriculture and fisheries sectors Creating a Multistakeholder Dialogue Forum for protected areas provides an avenue for rural workers’ organizations, producers’ organizations, and civil society organizations to participate in social and policy dialogue. This inclusion helps to ensure that the representation and empowerment of the rural poor, particularly women and youth, are considered in decision-making processes related to protected areas. Project Component 2. Nature-based Solutions in agriculture, fisheries and tourism sectors 2.1 Nature-based solutions for sustainable, inclusive, resilient, and productive ecosystems benefiting the agriculture, fisheries and tourism sectors 2.1.1-2.1.3 Participatory technical programs strengthened for transition to sustainable practices (agriculture, fisheries, tourism) Pillar 1 Employment creation and enterprise development Issue 1.1.1 Diagnosing the rural employment situation1.1.2 Pro-poor and gender-sensitive employment centred agricultural rural development polices and strategies 1.1.3 Value-chain development for decent work 1.2.1 Upgrading of small-scale agriculture 1.3.2 Rural people’s entrepreneurial and managerial skills 1.3.4 Group cooperation and producer organizations 1.4.1 Disaster risk management and climate change adaptation 1.5.1 Employment oriented training and agricultural education 1.6.1 Rural women and youth Conduct TAPE exercise to identify agroecological transition potential in target zones. Establish farmer field schools focused on converting to agroecological practices Establish demonstrations and pilot plots to showcase techniques suited to NbS (agroforestry, sustainable fisheries etc.) Strengthen farmer support systems (inputs, techniques, networks, demonstrations, organizational development) for climate resilient sustainable production Improve community-based and commercial fisheries management, aquaculture to ensure local fisheries-based food and nutrition security and improve income opportunities Conduct rapid diagnostic and provide organizational and administrative support to producers' associations that have the capacity to develop local development initiatives (circular economy, diversification, wholesale markets, collective bargaining approaches) Develop Action Plan for the implementation of artisanal fishing co-management in the target communities and fishing zones to support marine and coastal ecosystems Increase area of restoration in key watersheds through improved agricultural practices, and water conservation measures Support eco-tourism initiatives around coffee, cheese, fruits, and wine value chains in protected areas buffer zones This activity contributes to diagnosing the rural employment, and state of people’s livelihoods, by assessing the potential for transitioning to agroecological practices. Understanding the potential for such transitions helps identify opportunities for creating employment in sustainable agriculture. This exercise will also identify what are the most lucrative sustainable livelihoods that could potentially be invested in in the production side. Establishing farmer field schools helps implement pro-poor and gender-sensitive policies by providing training and support for small-scale farmers to adopt sustainable agricultural practices, leading to employment creation. Establishing demonstration and pilot plots to showcase techniques suited to NbS (agroforestry, sustainable fisheries etc/)supports value-chain development by showcasing sustainable techniques such as agroforestry and sustainable fisheries, which can create employment opportunities along the value chain. Strengthening support systems for small-scale farmers promotes the upgrading of small-scale agriculture by providing inputs, techniques, and organizational development support, leading to improved productivity and employment. Investments in improved management and NbS solutions will support individual fisherfolk to improve organizational capacity, coordination and potentially utilize collective bargaining to attain higher prices and greater revenue along the value chain. This activity enhances rural people’s entrepreneurial skills by providing support to producer associations, fostering organizational development, and promoting collective bargaining approaches. Issue This activity promotes group cooperation by developing action plans for artisanal fishing co-management, which involves local fishing communities and producer organizations in decision-making processes related to fisheries management. It invests in a more resilient sector contributing the social structures underpinning the local industry which can be quite atomized. Establishing demonstrations, improving fisheries management, and providing support to producer associations can specifically target rural women and youth, ensuring their inclusion and empowerment in employment and enterprise development initiatives. Increasing restoration in key watersheds and enhancing capacity building on ecosystems restoration contribute to disaster risk management and climate change adaptation, which indirectly supports sustainability of rural livelihoods. Supporting eco-tourism initiatives provides employment-oriented training and education opportunities in agricultural value chains, promoting rural employment and enterprise development. These activities collectively contribute to the FAO's objective of creating decent rural employment and fostering enterprise development by addressing various aspects of rural employment, including policy formulation, value-chain development, small-scale agriculture, skills development, and group cooperation, while also addressing issues related to disaster risk management, climate change adaptation, and the inclusion of rural women and youth 2.1.4 Restoration and sustainable use of prioritized grasslands, agricultural, coastal zones in protected areas and their buffer zones to maximize ecosystem services. Pillar 1 Employment creation and enterprise development Issue 1.2.1 Upgrading of small-scale agriculture Revegetate, reforest, re-green with endemic vegetation, indigenous trees and climate-resilient species in key watersheds, PA buffer zones and degraded areas Implement conservation of sand dunes, sea grasses and other coastal vegetation with support from private sector partners with alignment with tourism objectives Coral zones protection and rehabilitation Establish, support and upscale nurseries with native and climate-resilient species Upscale agroecological techniques for invasive species management, soil and water restoration All the restoration activities lead to indirect positive benefits. By increasing adaptive capacity, supporting biodiversity and soil health, activities seek to protect populations from degradation, erosion and climate disasters—thereby supporting more resilient livelihoods, especially for those dependent on the sustainability of natural resources. 2.2 Diversified livelihoods options scaled through NbS investments 2.2.1 Business Development for nature-positive initiatives linked to blue and green economy Foster and strengthen market linkages for small farmers, fisherfolks, connecting them with buyers, processors, and retailers, such as local markets, restaurants, and hotels Increase reliable and affordable access to agricultural inputs such as seeds, organic fertilizers, and pesticides Support administrative, organizational development to associations, and eco-tourism operators to upscale successful, sustainable initiatives and strengthen competencies of SMEs, strengthening their skills, develop producer associations (cooperatives), promote digital inclusion, innovation and circularity Assist small farmers and small food transformation folks in meeting quality standards and obtaining national certifications (sustainable production, pesticide free) Design innovative models for improved collective bargaining to improve sustainable livelihoods This activity directly contributes to value-chain development by identifying opportunities for investment in sustainable production, which can lead to the creation of decent work along the value chain. Supporting business development of women and youth promotes gender equality by providing them with opportunities in nature-positive initiatives, thereby enhancing their participation in rural employment. Strengthening market linkages and increasing access to agricultural inputs for small farmers contribute to upgrading small-scale agriculture, leading to improved productivity and employment opportunities. This activity supports the provision of reliable inputs which are essential for production and lovelihoods. By investing in more sustainable inputs, the project seeks to render livelihoods more resilient. This activity supports the upgrading of jobs and enterprises in the informal rural economy by strengthening the competencies of small and medium enterprises (SMEs), promoting digital inclusion, innovation, and circularity. Strengthening skills, developing producer associations, promoting digital inclusion, and meeting quality standards contribute to creating a favorable business environment for micro, small, and medium enterprises in the agribusiness sector. Supporting business development of women and youth, as well as strengthening their skills and competencies, directly address the inclusion and empowerment of rural women and youth in employment creation and enterprise development initiatives. These activities collectively contribute to the FAO’s objective of creating decent rural employment and fostering enterprise development by addressing various aspects such as value-chain development, gender equality, upgrading of small-scale agriculture, innovative employment mechanisms, business environment improvement, and support for rural women and youth. 3.1.3 Finance for Nature-Based Solutions accessible to MSMEs, smallholders and their associations Pillar 1 Employment creation and enterprise development Issue 1.2.1 Upgrading of small-scale agriculture 1.2.3 Innovative mechanisms for employment creation in rural areas 1.3.1 Business environment for micro, small and medium enterprises in agribusiness and marketing sector development 1.3.2 Rural people’s entrepreneurial and managerial skills 1.3.3 Supporting micro, small and medium enterprises in rural areas Create a financing window dedicated to NbS , gender and youth responsive and aligned with relevant legal and regulatory requirements, and best practices from government agencies, financial institutions, and development agencies. Provide matching grants for MSMEs, smallholders and their associations to: Investments associated with production (e.g. planting material for agroforestry, equipment for IPM, micro-irrigation systems, etc.) Investments related to storage facilities, and processing units to reduce post-harvest losses and enhance overall supply chain efficiency Provide financial literacy support to interested MSMEs, smallholders and their associations Creating a financing window dedicated to nature-based solutions (NbS) and providing matching grants for MSMEs and smallholders can support the upgrading of small-scale agriculture by facilitating access to finance for investments in production, storage, processing, and value addition. This can also promote innovative mechanisms for employment creation in rural areas by incentivizing investments in sustainable agriculture, processing facilities, and value addition, which can generate new job opportunities. This activity directly contributes to improving the business environment for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the agribusiness sector by providing a dedicated financing mechanism tailored to nature-based solutions, which can support their growth and development. Creating a financing window dedicated to NbS and providing matching grants for MSMEs and smallholders directly support these enterprises in rural areas by providing them with access to finance for investments in production, processing, and value addition, as well as by enhancing their capacity through financial literacy support. Investments supporting value addition in processing and packaging agricultural products to increase shelf life and create opportunities for higher-value sales Providing financial literacy support enhances rural people’s entrepreneurial and managerial skills by equipping them with the knowledge and skills needed to effectively manage finances, access credit, and make informed investment decisions. These activities collectively contribute to the FAO’s objective of creating decent rural employment and fostering enterprise development by addressing various aspects such as upgrading small-scale agriculture, innovative employment creation mechanisms, improving the business environment, enhancing entrepreneurial skills, and supporting rural enterprises. Project Component 3. Sustainable Green and Blue financial ecosystem 3.1 Sustainable finance for the Blue and Green economy sectors is effectively mobilized and channeled to expand Nature-based Solutions 3.1.1 National vehicles are operational to channel sustainable finance Pillar 1 Employment creation and enterprise development Issue 1.2.3 Innovative mechanisms for employment creation in rural areas 1.3.1 Business environment for micro, small and medium enterprises in agribusiness and marketing sector development Capacity development on Nature-based Solutions finance for the blue and green economy sectors Support the NFCN in establishing its resource mobilization strategy (RMS, while leveraging support from the Global BGI IP Support the NFCN to develop indicators for the Fund’s monitoring, verification and reporting framework These activities will strengthen the national finance mechanism issuing grants to smallholders, MSMEs and organizations seeking to pilot or integrate climate considerations into their activities. Strengthening vehicles to channel finance provides greater financial resources for rural actors to implement their sustainable activities, whose overhead may to be too high otherwise. 3.1.2 Micro Finance Institutions actively engage in the green/blue economy transition Pillar 1 Employment creation and enterprise development Issue 1.2.3 Innovative mechanisms for employment creation in rural areas 1.3.1 Business environment for micro, small and medium enterprises in agribusiness and marketing sector development Mainstream Green Microfinance principles into the MSME support system Development of innovative micro-finance products for the blue and green economy sectors Mainstreaming Green Microfinance principles and developing innovative micro-finance products for the blue and green economy sectors contribute to innovative mechanisms for employment creation in rural areas. By providing financial support tailored to sustainable initiatives, these activities encourage entrepreneurship and job creation in sectors aligned with environmental sustainability. Mainstreaming Green Microfinance principles and developing innovative micro-finance products also improve the business environment for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the agribusiness and marketing sectors. By offering financial products that support green and sustainable initiatives, these activities enable MSMEs to access capital for business expansion, investment in sustainable practices, and market development. These activities collectively contribute to the FAO’s objective of creating decent rural employment and fostering enterprise development by promoting innovative financing mechanisms that support green and sustainable initiatives, thereby enhancing employment opportunities and improving the business environment for rural enterprises. Project Component 4. Knowledge Management and Learning 4.1 Lessons from sustainable development initiatives captured, developed, and integrated by public, private and CSO sectors 4.1.1 Best practices from sustainable development initiatives leveraged by different users Pillar 1 Employment creation and enterprise development Issues 1.2.1 Upgrading of small-scale agriculture 1.2.3 Innovative mechanisms for employment creation in rural areas Develop a knowledge-sharing platform to disseminate lessons learned and best practices from the project to key stakeholders Develop sector-specific dissemination circles Experiences of NbS which yield improved livelihoods and socioeconomic development, will be disseminated to rural communities in ways they can access. 4.1.2 Multi-criteria assessment tools to capture/monitor change, lessons and practices for dissemination with the wider SIDS community Pillar 1 Employment creation and enterprise development Issues 1.2.1 Upgrading of small-scale agriculture 1.2.3 Innovative mechanisms for employment creation in rural areas Active engagement with global SIDS platforms and frameworks (e.g., BGI IP, SAMOA Pathway, SIDS Coalition for Nature) and other SIDS-relevant global processes and initiatives; Support existing intra-regional and global SIDS multi-stakeholder partnerships and governance entities to facilitate integrated interventions, sustained and scaled up action and build linkages with external platforms and initiatives Building linkages with external platforms and initiatives, can facilitate the exchange of ideas, resources, and best practices, leading to the implementation of innovative solutions that generate employment opportunities in rural communities. Multi-stakeholder partnerships can provide resources, knowledge, and technical support needed for small-scale farmers to adopt modern technologies, improve productivity, and access markets

The proposed project will accelerate Cabo Verde's transition to green and blue economy, transforming agriculture, fisheries and tourism sectors to conserve and sustain the archipelago's unique marine and terrestrial ecosystems, as these sectors support the country's wealth and depend on healthy and productive terrestrial and marine ecosystems. Indicators: # of direct beneficiaries (disaggregated by sex) # of NBS initiatives that have been upscaled in terms of (1) financial growth, (2) geographic scope, and (3) sectoral scope (supports BGI IP Tier 2 indicator 2.1.1 for the transformation lever on Governance Policies, GCP indicator 2)
